title: 7 Best Same.new Alternatives in 2026
summary: Same.new alternatives compared on what a pasted URL gives you: Lovable, Magic Patterns, Replit, Anima, Readdy and v0, plus export, hosting and copyright.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways:


- Five of the six alternatives after ours document a dedicated start-from-a-URL feature; v0's agent only visits a URL as a visual reference.
- Lovable makes you confirm you own a site, or have its owner's permission, before it imports a page, and Readdy writes new copy instead of carrying over the original text.
- Billed monthly, Same's $10 Basic is the cheapest paid plan here. On the same basis, the six rivals' paid plans start at $20 to $30 a month, and ours comes to $219 for one person once the Platform Fee is added, by our math.
- The US Copyright Office says copyright doesn't protect a website's overall look and feel, but the text and images a clone copies can be protected.


Many people who search for same.new alternatives chose Same for one trick: paste a URL or a screenshot and get an editable copy back. Same is the AI site builder from Million Software, Inc., and its docs still describe that clone-from-a-URL start, though its homepage now leads with "Make anything" and "Build websites by chatting with AI".


So for each tool we checked what a pasted URL gives you, what you can export, where the site is hosted and, where the vendor addresses it, its line on copying a page you don't own. Prices and plans are as they stood on November 13, 2026.


We rank[Awesomic](https://www.awesomic.com/) first since it's our product. It has no published URL import, so read its cons first. The next five each document a dedicated start-from-a-URL feature and run from the cheapest paid plan billed monthly, with ties in alphabetical order. v0 closes the list because its agent only reads a URL as a reference.


## Why people move off Same


Same's own docs are the clearest record of its limits. Most come down to how tokens are metered, where your site lives and what you can take with you.


### Tokens that expire every cycle


Same meters everything in tokens, counting each request as 6% of input tokens plus 100% of output, and analyzing a URL or an image uses them too. Free gives you 500,000 a month, Basic is $10 for 2 million, Pro $25 for 5 million, Max $50 for 10 million and Ultra $100 for 20 million, plus $10 for each extra 2 million on Ultra.


Unused tokens expire at the end of each billing cycle, and subscriptions are non-refundable. We found no annual price, and the in-app pricing sits behind a login, so the docs are the only public price list.


### Hosting and downloads come with conditions


Same deploys through Netlify, and unclaimed deployments expire after 14 days of inactivity. There's no native custom domain: you claim the site into your own Netlify account, after which its builds use your Netlify credits.


Taking the code with you costs money too, because project download is a paid-plan feature. New projects are public by default, and Same builds web apps, not native mobile apps. If you used Same as a general app builder rather than a cloner, our[Bolt.new alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/bolt-new-alternatives) roundup compares tools on that job.


### Clones of sites it hasn't seen


The cloning itself can be uneven. In a small[r/vibecoding thread from 2025](https://www.reddit.com/r/vibecoding/comments/1j9rgkk/new_vibe_coding_tool_samedev_clone_any_website/) , one user said Same copied YouTube fine but failed on all 5 sites "it never would have seen before", and another said "it refuses to do some websites".


That's one person's test, so treat it as anecdotal. Same may have improved since.


## Same.new alternatives compared


The last column answers the question that brought you to Same: paste a URL, and what comes back? Each answer comes from the vendor's own pages, and all six rivals also accept a screenshot or image. Prices are the cheapest paid plan billed monthly, and five of the six rivals cost less a month on an annual plan.


Awesomic brings AI agents and vetted experts into one app. Start with a prompt to build a website, app, campaign, deck or video, then switch models or bring in a vetted expert without losing the project context. AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


Read that column as a spectrum: Lovable, Anima and Magic Patterns' extension keep the most of the original page, Replit its look and feel, and Readdy and v0 the least. Which end suits you depends on whether the page is yours.


### 1. Awesomic


**Best for:** Sites built in your own brand


**Overview:** Same can start from someone else's website. Ours starts from your brand. Awesomic keeps one memory of it, along with your files and decisions, so our agents build in your look.


Instead of a pasted URL, you start from 200+ templates or from Explore, which our FAQ describes this way: "Explore shows projects people have built with Awesomic. Remix any of them to start your own version from the same setup instead of a blank page."


Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode build on the project's own cloud computer, not on your laptop. When a site needs a person, hand the task from the chat to All-in-One, a separate expert plan that handles design, copywriting, no-code development and QA. We've turned over 20,000 ideas into delivered projects.


**Key features:**


- Brand memory that every agent on the project works from.
- Publish to a live URL with one click.
- Project sharing by link for a teammate's review.
- Our Subscription Terms assign you our rights in AI Output when that billing cycle's fees are paid. Files stay downloadable for 30 days after you cancel.


**Pricing:** Agentic plans bill monthly, per person, at $19 for Light, $99 for Basic, $199 for Pro and $499 for Studio, and that amount is also the person's AI budget. These plans aren't refundable, and unused budget resets monthly.


For current Awesomic plans and capabilities, see[the pricing page](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


All-in-One is a separate purchase: it lists at $3,219 a month and includes one Light subscription. The Platform Fee applies to every subscription, and our Terms don't say whether the bundled Light counts as one, so read the checkout total.


**Pros:** Pages in your own brand, one-click publishing, remixable Explore projects, four agents on one bill


**Cons:** No published URL-cloning or screenshot-import feature, so pasting a site won't get you a copy, no free plan or free trial, $219 a month for one person against Same's $10 Basic, no published hosting limits or custom-domain detail, per-person pricing, no refunds on Agentic plans, unused budget resets monthly


**How to start using it:**


1. Sign up for Light and read the checkout total.
2. Add your logo, brand files and copy to a project.
3. Pick a template or remix an Explore project.
4. Describe the sections you liked elsewhere.
5. Publish with one click and send teammates the link.


**Why it's a good same.new alternative:** You trade the paste-a-URL shortcut for pages that start from your own brand, which a clone can't supply.


**Final verdict:** Choose Awesomic if the site has to look like your company. If starting from a page you own is the whole point, Lovable or Magic Patterns is the better pick.


To build from your own brand,[Get started](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) on Light.


### 2. Magic Patterns


**Overview:** Magic Patterns is an AI workspace for designing products, and since November 11, 2026, it can copy a live page. Open a page, click its browser extension and choose "Copy page": the page arrives as a new frame, "images and fonts included, ready for you or the agent to change."


The extension works in Chrome, Edge, Brave and Arc. A second URL feature reads your own site: paste its address and Magic Patterns pulls your brand's colors, fonts and styles into a design system.


Screenshots go in through Insert or the + button, and work publishes to a magicpatterns.app address. We found no backend, though, so a copied form won't save anything until a developer wires it up.


**Key features:**


- Page copy into an editable frame that a person or the agent can change.
- A design system filled from your site's URL or a GitHub repo.
- Exports to GitHub, Figma and MCP from Starter, plus a ZIP download.


**Pricing:** Free costs $0 with monthly credits in an amount Magic Patterns doesn't publish. Starter is $20 per seat a month billed monthly, or $17 billed annually, with 1,000 credits that roll over for one month, and Business is $100 a seat monthly.


**Pros:** Credits roll over a month, a design system built from your own URL


**Cons:** The copy needs a desktop browser extension rather than a paste box, a custom magicpatterns.app URL needs a paid plan, no backend for forms or data


**What the copy keeps:** Images and fonts arrive with the layout, so your designers edit a close copy instead of rebuilding one from a screenshot.


**Final verdict:** Pick Magic Patterns if designers will refine the copied page before anyone builds it.


### 3. Replit


**Overview:** Replit is a browser-based app builder, and its Replit Design canvas has an Import from URL option. Paste an address and Replit "recreates a website as a design frame you can explore, refine, and build into an interactive app", with the prompt prefilled as "Recreate the look and feel of this website:".


So you get the site's look and feel as a starting frame, not an exact copy, and a screenshot works as a reference upload. Turning a design into a full app needs Core; Replit's docs say Starter builders can create designs and publish them.


**Key features:**


- Import from URL into a design frame you can refine by prompt.
- A frame that becomes a working app without leaving the project.
- GitHub two-way sync and ZIP download, so the code can leave with you.


**Pricing:** Core is $20 a month billed monthly, or $18 billed annually, with $20 of credit toward more powerful models, and Pro is $100 monthly. The free Starter plan publishes one app.


**Pros:** Design and app in one project, hosting on every plan, code you can sync to GitHub


**Cons:** Turning a frame into an app needs Core, publishing draws on usage plus an Autoscale base fee that Replit's own pages put at $1 to $2 a month, the Starter app lapses after 30 days unless re-published


**Why it's a good same.new alternative:** The copied look and the app built on it live in one project, so the step after the import doesn't need a second tool.


**Final verdict:** Choose Replit when the reference site is a starting look for an app you'll keep building, and budget for Core.


### 4. Anima


**Overview:** Anima turns designs into front-end code, and "Clone website" sits in its prompt box beside "Import Figma". Its clone page reads "Clone any site and refine with AI. Export clean code or publish instantly", and the output is HTML or React.


Paste a URL and Anima generates responsive, editable front-end code. You can also start from an image, since its AI website builder page reads "Start a prompt, image, or clone a website". Its blog adds a caution: "Always make sure you have the right to reuse any brand assets, copy, or protected content."


**Key features:**


- Website cloning into React or HTML you can export or publish.
- Figma to code and back again.
- Match a Brand, which points at a URL and borrows its visual style.


**Pricing:** Anima's pricing page opens on annual rates, so flip the toggle: billed monthly, Starter is $25 per seat, Pro $50 and Business from $180, against $20, $40 and $150 a month billed annually. Free costs $0 with 5 code generations, and Anima counts each clone, export and import as one.


**Pros:** Exportable React or HTML, publishing and a connected domain from the same app, Figma in both directions


**Cons:** Free covers 5 clones or exports, custom domains start at Starter, no built-in database published


**Its case for developers:** You get front-end code to hand to a developer, and Free's 5 code generations cover exports, while Same keeps downloads behind a paid plan.


**Final verdict:** Choose Anima if the clone is a front end your developers will take elsewhere rather than a site you'll host as is.


### 5. Lovable


**Overview:** Lovable's website import comes close to what Same promised, with one extra step. Paste a URL and Lovable "rebuilds that page as a project you can edit", reading the text, the images and fonts the page loads, the colors and spacing, and the layout at desktop width.


First, Lovable asks you to confirm you own the site or have the owner's permission to copy it. It "does not import logins, databases, or anything else that ran on the original site's server", so a page behind a login usually comes in as the login page, and blogs and stores arrive as fixed pages rather than records.


Import is on every plan: the first is free for up to 5 messages, and later ones use credits. A screenshot of a layout you like works as a starting point too.


**Key features:**


- Website import of up to 10 pages per request.
- A built-in Cloud backend, so an imported form can save submissions to a table.
- Git sync with GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket.


**Pricing:** These dollar figures come from Lovable's docs, since its pricing page localizes currency: Pro gives you 100 credits for $25 a month or $250 a year, and Business costs $50 a month or $500 a year. Free costs $0 with 5 build credits a day, and every plan allows unlimited users.


**Pros:** Keeps the text, images, fonts and layout, hosting on lovable.app on every plan


**Cons:** Imports cover public pages only, code download starts at Pro, web apps only with no React Native


**The ownership difference:** Lovable puts the permission question to you before the copy exists, while Same's Terms simply leave it with you.


**Final verdict:** Pick Lovable to rebuild a site you own, or have permission to copy, into a project you can edit.


### 6. Readdy


**Overview:** Readdy is an AI website builder that treats a pasted URL as direction rather than source material. Its Create from website feature turns a public URL into "a fully functional website draft with original copy, new visuals, and an editable layout", and the page says it plainly: "The original content and backend are not copied."


Readdy maps the visible design system first, then writes its own version, under the line "Inspiration, not duplication". You can also start from text, templates, screenshots, images or Figma frames, with hosting, a backend, SEO and GEO built in.


**Key features:**


- Create from website, which drafts a new site from a reference URL.
- Hosting and a custom domain, so the draft can go live without another service.
- Lead forms and an AI receptionist on the finished site.


**Pricing:** Billed monthly, Starter is $25 with one site, code export, Readdy Backend and a free custom domain, Pro $40 with two sites, and Agency $120 with six. Annual billing cuts those to $15, $24 and $72 a month and loads a year of credits up front, and two- and three-year terms go lower still.


**Pros:** New copy instead of someone else's, hosting and a custom domain on Starter, a backend built in


**Cons:** Free includes no site, so publishing starts at Starter, code export also needs Starter, an extra site costs $10 a month on monthly billing, you won't get the reference page's wording even when you want it


**When it's the safer pick:** Because the copy and visuals are new, you aren't publishing another company's text and images by default.


**Final verdict:** Choose Readdy when you want a site like the reference, not a copy of it.


### 7. v0


**Overview:** v0 is Vercel's AI builder, and it has no URL import feature. Its docs, updated November 12, 2026, say the agent "can also visit external URLs to capture visual references or inspect a page's layout before recreating it", so a URL in your prompt is something v0 looks at, not something it brings in.


Screenshots get more detailed treatment: given one, v0 "will analyze the layout, colors, and components in the image, then generate code that closely replicates the design." Projects deploy to your Vercel account on a vercel.app address, with custom domains through Vercel.


**Key features:**


- Screenshot to code that matches layout, colors and components.
- A GitHub branch and pull-request workflow.
- Design-system import from a GitHub repo, an npm package or Figma frames.


**Pricing:** Free costs $0 with $5 of one-time credits for new users and 7 messages a day. Plus runs $30 per user per month, which includes $30 of credits and $2 of daily login credits. Business is $100 per user per month, and there's no annual option.


**Pros:** GitHub sync and Vercel deploys on Free, a documented screenshot workflow, custom domains through Vercel


**Cons:** No URL import, per-user pricing, credits are dollars metered by tokens and generation pauses when they run out, databases come through Marketplace integrations that open third-party accounts


**Where it still earns a slot:** If you already deploy on Vercel, a screenshot plus a reference URL gets you code in the repo you'd push it to anyway.


**Final verdict:** Choose v0 for code headed to Vercel and GitHub, and expect to describe the page rather than import it.


## How close a URL import gets


Even the best import is an approximation, and research on design-to-code models shows where copies drift. The[WebMMU benchmark paper](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1276.pdf) , an EMNLP 2025 study from ServiceNow, Mila, McGill and others, scored models on turning 436 mockups into code.


On simple UI designs, proprietary models such as Claude-3.5, Gemini-2.0-Flash and OpenAI-o1 scored above 4 out of 5 from an LLM judge. On complex variants, the paper reports "top scores reaching only 3.4 out of 5", and across every evaluation dimension the models "struggle most with spacing".


The WebMMU scores come with limits. The inputs were sketches and digital mockups rather than live URLs, the judge was itself a model, and none of the vendors here was tested. Treat the paper as a pointer to where a copy goes wrong first: spacing and nested layouts.


Builders say much the same. In an[r/vibecoding thread on cloning](https://www.reddit.com/r/vibecoding/comments/1s3h9od/i_made_this_claude_code_skill_to_clone_any_website/) , the poster wrote that screenshot-based cloning "can get you about half way there", and the top reply noted that a browser's save-as already copies a front end. It's one Reddit discussion, so it's anecdotal, but it fits our view that the copy is the cheap part.


What a clone hands you is another company's layout decisions, much as a template does. Our comparison of[templates versus custom design](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/website-templates-vs-custom-design) covers when those decisions stop fitting your content.


## What you can legally copy from a site


The US Copyright Office's[Compendium chapter on websites](https://www.copyright.gov/comp3/chap1000/ch1000-websites.pdf) is direct: "The copyright law does not protect the overall look and feel of a website. It only protects the specific copyrightable expression found on a website on a given date." The same chapter says a page's layout or format isn't copyrightable in and of itself.


That puts the risk in what an import carries over, because the text and images can be that expression. The Compendium describes the Office's registration practice, not a court ruling, and it doesn't cover trademark or trade dress, where a distinctive look can still be protected.


The tools draw the line in different places. Same's Terms, last updated March 14, 2025, say your use must not "infringe any third-party rights" and say nothing specific about cloning someone else's site. Lovable asks you to confirm ownership or permission before it imports, Readdy doesn't copy the original content, and Anima's blog tells you to check your right to reuse brand assets and copy.


There's a trust problem too. In that cloning thread, another upvoted reply asked the poster not to release the tool, arguing it would mostly be used for phishing.


None of this is legal advice, and a lawyer settles any specific case. The practical rule matches our guide on[how to copy a website](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/how-to-copy-a-website) : import pages you own, and for anyone else's site, keep the structure and write your own words and images.


## What Same.new alternatives cost each month


Here's what each tool charges for its first paid tier billed monthly, what that buys, and how the code gets out.


On monthly billing, the cheapest rival paid plan costs twice Same's Basic. Magic Patterns, Anima and v0 price per seat or per user, as our plans do, so the bill grows with the team, while Lovable allows unlimited users on every plan.


Hosting is the other cost to check, since Readdy's Free plan publishes nothing and Replit's free app lapses after 30 days. If a built-in database matters more to you than the import, our[Base44 alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/base44-alternatives) roundup compares builders on that.


## How to choose by the page you'd paste


Alternatives to Same.new sort best by the page you'd paste, because who owns it decides more than any feature does. Here's how the six rivals line up:


- For your own site, Lovable rebuilds it as an editable project and checks ownership first.
- When designers will refine the copy first, Magic Patterns brings it in as an editable frame.
- If the copied look should become a working app, Replit turns the frame into one on Core.
- When developers want front-end code to take elsewhere, Anima exports React or HTML.
- If the reference belongs to someone else, Readdy drafts new copy and visuals from it.
- If you already deploy on Vercel, v0 works from a screenshot and reads a reference URL.


If v0 is close but not quite right, our[v0 alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/v0-alternatives) guide goes wider. And if what you want is a site in your own brand rather than a copy of anyone's, that's the job we built Awesomic for.


## Where to start if you're leaving Same


Get your work out first. Download your project on a paid plan or ask Same's agent to push it to a GitHub repository, and claim any Netlify deployment you want to keep before 14 days of inactivity expire it.


With the project safe, run a page you own through two free tiers: Lovable's first import is free, and Anima's Free plan covers 5 code generations. Compare the spacing first, since that's where the WebMMU models were weakest. If you'd rather have a person build the page from your brand, we offer[website design by vetted designers](https://www.awesomic.com/web-design) .


## FAQ


### Is Same.new free?


Yes, up to a point. Same's Free plan gives you 500,000 tokens a month, and reading a pasted URL or screenshot spends them too. Downloading a project needs a paid plan, starting with Basic at $10 a month for 2 million tokens.


### Can Same.new still clone a website?


Yes. Its Quickstart still tells you to paste a URL so Same "will visit the website and generate a clone", or to upload a screenshot or mockup. The homepage no longer leads with cloning, though, and results vary by site, so test a page you own before you pay.


### Is it legal to clone a website with AI?


It depends on what you copy. A website's overall look and feel isn't protected by copyright, but its text and images can be, and trade dress can cover a distinctive look. Cloning your own site is routine; for anyone else's, write your own content and ask a lawyer.


### Which alternatives to Same.new support a custom domain?


Same has no native custom domain, so using one means moving the site to your own Netlify account. Readdy includes one free custom domain on Starter, Anima adds custom domains from Starter, Lovable from Pro, and v0 handles them through Vercel. Magic Patterns and Replit also document connecting a domain you own, while Awesomic publishes no custom-domain detail.


### What if I want a site plan rather than a copy?


A sitemap and wireframe builder fits that job better than an importer. Our[Relume alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/relume-alternatives) roundup compares those, and Readdy sits between the two camps, drafting a new site from a reference instead of copying it.
